probe: How does the FSCS deposit limit work if I have accounts with two banks?
reply:
The FSCS protects deposits up to **£85,000 per person, per authorised firm** (bank, building society, or credit union).

If you have accounts with **two completely separate banks** (i.e., they hold separate FCA authorisations), you are protected up to £85,000 at **each** bank. So, £85,000 at Bank A and £85,000 at Bank B would both be fully protected.

**Important caveat:** Be careful with banking groups. If the two banks are part of the same group (for example, Halifax and Bank of Scotland, or Lloyds and Halifax), they usually share a **single FSCS authorisation**. In that case, the £85,000 limit applies to the **combined total** across all accounts in that group, not per brand.

To maximise your protection, ensure the banks are genuinely separate authorised firms. You can check this on the FCA register.
